requirement:
This project's CI generates Rustdoc for the workspace before building the book.
The published documentation includes both the book and that generated Rustdoc
site in the same GitHub Pages deployment under
{cite}`requirements.integration.ci`. The appendix contains a "Rustdocs" entry
opening the `habeas_sdk` crate's documentation under
{cite}`requirements.index.rustdocs`.
rationale:
The one marked test, `tests/rustdocs.rs#fn[rustdocs_ci_generates_workspace_site_before_building_the_published_book]`, covers every obligation that `requirements.index.rustdocs.publication` states itself.

- **Rustdoc is generated for the workspace before the book is built.** The test parses `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. It finds the step that runs `cargo doc --locked --workspace --no-deps` and the step that runs `mdbook build`. It asserts the doc step comes before the build step. An implementation that dropped the doc step, narrowed it to one crate, or moved it after the book build would fail.
- **Both are published in the same GitHub Pages deployment.** The test asserts that the `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4` step comes after the build step and uploads `book`. The Rustdoc site is imported into `book/rustdocs/` by the preprocessor, so one artifact carries both. That the imported site lands under `rustdocs/` belongs to `requirements.index.rustdocs`, which is cited only as context. The deploy-on-`main` and check-job gating belong to `requirements.integration.ci`, also cited only as context.
- **The appendix has a "Rustdocs" entry that opens the `habeas_sdk` docs.** The test takes the part of `md/SUMMARY.md` after `# Appendix` and asserts it contains `[Rustdocs](./rustdocs.md)`. It asserts `md/rustdocs.md` consists exactly of the `:::{rustdocs}` / `:::` directive. It also asserts that `book.toml` sets `preprocessor.habeas.rustdocs.crate` to `habeas_sdk` and `path` to `target/doc`. Together these show the entry is a navigation chapter pointing at the `habeas_sdk` crate's documentation.

The remaining behavior in the cited `requirements.index.rustdocs` and `requirements.integration.ci` is context, not part of this subject's assessment. I found no relevant untested clause and no plausible violation the assertions would accept. An optional extra check on the `output.habeas.command` setting does no harm.

text: :::{req} rustdocs.publication
This project's CI generates Rustdoc for the workspace before building the book.
The published documentation includes both the book and that generated Rustdoc
site in the same GitHub Pages deployment under
{cite}`requirements.integration.ci`. The appendix contains a "Rustdocs" entry
opening the `habeas_sdk` crate's documentation under
{cite}`requirements.index.rustdocs`.
:::{req} ci

A GitHub Actions CI workflow MUST run, for pull requests and pushes to `main`, these checks: `cargo habeas coverage -- --locked --workspace` under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.run`, `cargo test --locked --doc --workspace`, `mdbook test`, the autofix controller tests with `node --test .github/scripts/autofix.test.mjs`, and, in a separate job, the Symposium session-start hook smoke test `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`. It also builds the book as documentation under {cite}`requirements.index.render_only`, without requiring collected execution reports for rendering. On a push to `main`, only after every check job passes, it deploys the generated `book/` directory to GitHub Pages. The book MUST set `output.html.site-url` to `/habeas-codicem/` for project-site hosting.
::::{req} rustdocs
A book can import a generated Rustdoc site through its Habeas preprocessor
configuration:
```toml
[preprocessor.habeas.rustdocs]
path = "target/doc"
crate = "habeas_sdk"
`path` identifies the generated documentation directory relative to the project
root; `crate` selects the landing page at `<crate>/index.html`. A chapter
consisting of one closed, standalone `{rustdocs}` directive with an empty body
becomes a navigation entry into that crate's Rustdoc site. The directive opens
with at least three colons and closes with at least as many:
```text
:::{rustdocs}
The built book includes the imported site under `rustdocs/`, preserving its
pages, assets, search data, and links. Selecting the chapter opens the native
Rustdoc page in the same tab, with Rustdoc's own layout and navigation. Relative
links from book chapters to imported item pages resolve when the publication is
hosted under a URL prefix.
The build reports a readable error if the directive has no import configuration, the
configured directory, crate landing page, or any imported site file cannot be
read, the import fails, or an imported file would overwrite a book output file.
